demandSource: DataForSEO US 2026-10-28: rent vs buy calculator 14,800/mo KD 49 (reports/mindmap-pass/2026-10-28-autocomplete-run/volumes.json)
decisionGap: Site has a qualitative renting-vs-buying explainer but no way to compute a personal break-even.
sampledAlternatives: SERP 2026-10-28 (serp.json): bank and credit-union calculators, NYT; AI Overview cites NerdWallet, calculator.net, Zillow, NYT. Small sample, no uniqueness claim.
method: Month-by-month simulation of buying vs renting and investing the same cash; one-assumption-at-a-time scenarios. Python reference (check.py -> check.out.json) and TypeScript engine (src/lib/rent-vs-buy.ts) agree on all 18 scenarios (ts_check.out.txt).
assumptions: Planning assumptions (not sourced facts): property tax 1.0%, insurance 0.5%, maintenance 1.0%, closing 3%, selling 6%, home growth 3%, rent growth 3%, investment return 6%, renter insurance $15, PMI 0.5% while LTV above 80% with under 20% down.

findings.label: modeled
findings.text: Default case: break-even year 21; renting and investing ahead by $41,156 after 7 years.

findings.label: modeled
findings.text: Rate 5% -> break-even year 5; rate 6% -> year 8; rate 4% -> year 4.

findings.label: modeled
findings.text: Never within 30 years at 1% home growth or 9% investment return.

counterexample: Lower rate, higher rent, or faster home growth flips the default verdict (scenarios in check.out.json).
unknowns: Future home prices, rents, returns and local costs; income-tax effects of owning are not modeled.

provenance.scopeAndLimits: Modeled scenarios, not measured, not a forecast; no product tested, no client record.
